title: AtkinsLab @ VCU
text:
Silva et al. 2026: Led by Dr. Carlos Silva (U of Florida), PI on our ICESat-2/NASA grant, we detail the uses of ICESat-2 data beyond the ice, cloud, and elevation applications it was designed for. This work was funded by the NASA ICESat-2 program and published in IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine



Crockett et al. 2026: Published in Ecology Letters this past spring and led by former postdoc, now University of Northern British Columbia professor Erin Crockett, we used FIA and GEDI data to show connections between forest species diversity and resistance to drought. This work was funded by the USDA Forest Service.



Atkins et al. 2025: We recently published a data paper in JGR-Biogeosciences outlining methods behind the determination of aboveground woody biomass for all 35 NEON sites populated by woody tree species. This work was in part funded by the USDA Forest Service was in partnership with collaborators at NEON, VCU, and Oklahoma State University.
For a full and up-to-date list of publications, visit the Jeff Atkins Google Scholar page.

title: AtkinsLab @ VCU
text:
The Atkins Lab is rooted in a fundamental question: how is the natural world built, and what does that mean for ecosystem function? We seek to understand how the physical and spatial structure of ecosystems influences the movement of energy and matter across scales - from the local scale to entire landscapes.
Our research foci include watershed biogeochemistry, ecohydrology, remote sensing, forest structure analysis, quantitative ecology, and carbon and water cycling dynamics. Our work is integrative and systems-based, combining multiple data sources and methodologies including modeling, remote sensing, field measurements, manipulative experiments, and long-term datasets.
Beyond conducting research, we are committed to building open-source tools for the scientific community - R packages, dashboards, and datasets - engaging with stakeholders and policymakers, and fostering collaboration across disciplines and international borders. We believe the most pressing questions in ecosystem science require moving beyond disciplinary boundaries, and that scientific insight must ultimately inform land management and policy decisions.

title: AtkinsLab @ VCU
text:
Beginning summer 2026, we will be collecting field and remote sensing data at the Rice Rivers Center in order to build a digital twin of the forest ecosystem as a teaching and research tool. More to come!



An ongoing, DOE-BER funded project centered around a large-scale, wildfire simulation experiment where 100s of acres of southern forests were burned at the Savannah River Site under intensive fuel-load manipulations.



ICESat4D is a research project funded by NASA’s ICESat2 program and led by PI Carlos Silva at the Forest Biometrics, Remote Sensing, and AI Lab (SilvaLab) at the University of Florida in partnership with the USDA Forest Service, Jones Center at Ichauway & VCU. This project aims to understand the impact of hurricane disturbance on forest structure and AGBD resistance and recovery using ICESat-2 data combined with passive optical and SAR data, advanced statistical modeling methods, and a process-based Ecosystem Demography Model (EDv2.2) in southern forests in Florida and Georgia.










At left, the study area (36,218.00 km2) of the proposed work highlighted by the Florida Forest Service estimates of timber damage severity from Hurricane Michael. Study sites for data collection: Apalachicola National Forest (ANF) and the Forestland Group (FGL) forests in FL, and the Jones Ecological Research Center (JERC) at Ichauway in GA. At right, ALS Pre- and post-hurricane Michael derived canopy cover estimates.

title: AtkinsLab @ VCU
text:
Collaborations

CMS4D: A Multi-Scale Data Fusion Prototype System for the next Generation of Carbon Dynamics Monitoring from Space: A Case Study in the Brazilian Cerrado – Fire and Fuel in a Biodiversity Hotspot
CMS4D is a research project funded by NASA’s Carbon Monitoring System program and led by PI Carlos Silva at the Forest Biometrics, Remote Sensing, and AI Lab (SilvaLab) at the University of Florida. It started in August 2023 and is scheduled to last for a duration of 3 years. CMS4D is built upon pioneering work led by Dr. Carine Klauberg in the Brazilian Cerrado during 2019-2021 through a project funded by the National Council for Scientific and Technological Development (CNPq) - PrevFogo program.
